name: Kalaiyappar Temple, Kalaiyarkoil
deity: Shiva as Kalaiyappar (Swarnakaleeswarar), with the goddess Sornavalli (Soundaranayaki)
period: Ancient Shaiva shrine of the Pandya country, the Tirukkanapper of the Tevaram (8th century); towers and renewals of the Pandya and later Marudhu Pandiyar eras
dynasty: Pandya origins, with later renewal by the Marudhu Pandiyar rulers of Sivagangai
summary: Kalaiyappar Temple at Kalaiyarkoil, the Tirukkanapper of the Tevaram, is a Shiva shrine of the Pandya country with three sanctums beneath a towering nine-tiered gopuram, remembered also for the Marudhu Pandiyar brothers who renewed it.

sections.history: Kalaiyarkoil in Sivagangai district is the Tirukkanapper of the Tevaram, and its Shiva temple is a Paadal Petra Sthalam of the Pandya country. The place is also named Tirukkanapper in the Sangam anthology Purananuru, which shows how old the name is. Tradition recalls a visit by the saint Sundarar to the shrine. In the late eighteenth century the town was the seat of the Marudhu Pandiyar brothers, Periya Marudhu and Chinna Marudhu, who ruled the Sivagangai country and resisted the British. They are remembered for renewing the temple within their fort and raising a lofty gopuram for it, and a memorial to them stands on the street facing the main tower.
sections.architecture: Two east-facing gopurams rise over the temple: a nine-tiered tower of about 150 to 157 feet, among the tallest in Tamil Nadu, and a smaller five-tiered one. Sources differ on who built which, crediting the Marudhu brothers, the Pandya king Sundara Pandiyan, or both, so the attribution is best held as traditional. Within two prakarams stand three separate sanctums: Swarnakaleeswarar at the centre, Someswarar on the right and Sundareswarar on the left. The goddess Sornavalli, known also as Soundaranayaki, has her own shrine. Tradition says that from the top of the great tower the gopuram of the Meenakshi temple at Madurai could once be seen.
sections.legends: The name Swarnakaleeswarar, the Lord of gold, recalls the tale of a Pandya king who had no child. His queen, to console herself, fashioned the image of a child in gold. The king is said to have later raised the temple around that sacred spot in remembrance of these events. The tale is told as tradition, and its details vary from one telling to another. Later memory has joined the temple to the Marudhu Pandiyars, whose renewal of it is recalled in the town to this day.
sections.festivals: The main festival of the Lord falls in the Tamil month of Thai, in January or February, when the chariot festival is held on the Poosam star. Someswarar's Brahmotsavam is celebrated in the month of Vaikasi, in May or June, and Aadi Pooram, in July or August, is observed for the goddess Swarnavalli. Each year on 27 October the town keeps Marudhu Pandiyar Guru Pooja in honour of the Marudhu brothers. Maha Shivaratri and the monthly Pradosham are observed as at every Shiva temple. Confirm dates locally, as they follow the Tamil calendar.
sections.experience: Kalaiyarkoil rewards a patient visit. The great nine-tiered tower announces the temple from a distance, and the street before it holds the memorial of the Marudhu brothers. Pass beneath the gopuram and visit the three sanctums in turn, beginning with Swarnakaleeswarar at the centre. Offer your respects to the goddess Sornavalli in her shrine, then walk the prakarams slowly, thinking of the kings and saints who have passed here. The festival months bring the largest crowds, and the quieter hours outside them suit a calm darshan.

visit.timings: Typically open in the morning and again from late afternoon into the evening, with a midday break; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected: dhotis or trousers for men, sarees, salwar kameez, or long skirts for women, with shoulders and knees covered. Footwear is left at the entrance stands.
visit.photography: Photography is generally permitted in the outer corridors and courtyards but prohibited inside the inner sanctum, in keeping with Tamil Nadu temple rules. Ask temple staff before photographing rituals or priests.
visit.gettingThere: Kalaiyarkoil is a town in Sivagangai district, reached by road from Sivagangai, Madurai and Karaikudi. Madurai has the nearest major airport, and Madurai, Sivagangai and Karaikudi all have railway stations. Buses serve the town, and the tall gopuram is easy to spot on arrival. Confirm routes and distances locally before travelling.
